payload.title: Web of Shadows
payload.blurb: New York, present day. When Thanos came, every Avenger who was not a spider-person died in the fighting: Tony Stark, Steve Rogers, Thor and the rest of the team are gone, and their tower stands empty over Midtown. What keeps the city running now is a small group of spider-people, Peter Parker, Gwen…
payload.overview:
New York City, present day. The subway runs on a cut timetable, and power is reliable only in Midtown and the Financial District, so the outer boroughs live by generator and candlelight after dark. The police still patrol, but they are short of officers and short of trust. The National Guard holds the bridges and the tunnels. The emergency panel sends the spider-powered to the places where the city is failing, and most of them answer the call anyway.

Powers in this city are rare and physical: strength, climbing, a sense that warns of danger a second before it arrives, and webbing from the wrists or a hidden gland. Spider-people are ordinary people who got lucky once and have paid for it since. Nobody here carries a status panel, a rank, or a number that says what they can do. There are no levels, classes or status windows here.

Money is cash, favors and ration cards. The big shops on Fifth Avenue still take cards, and corner stores take whatever the neighborhood trusts. People in Hell's Kitchen pay the collectors weekly and do not talk about it. Campus life goes on, with classes, dorms and a library that stays open late, but nobody walks home alone after dark.
payload.intro:
Pryce Hall smells like wet wool and dry-erase marker. At the front, Peter Parker stands with his back to the room, sleeves pushed past the elbows, writing an equation in a hand that shakes a little at the bottom of the board. Fresh grey scrapes mark the knuckles of his right hand. When he turns, his eyes go to the back row first and then to you, the way a man checks a street before he crosses it.

Peter says there will be a quiz today, which is a lie you can read on his face. Gwen Stacy is not in the room, but a grey coat hangs over the back of her seat in the third row. Miles Morales leans across the aisle to whisper that his blue hoodie is still missing from the gym.

When the bell goes, Peter caps the marker and says, quietly, 'Stay behind a minute.' He is already looking at the door.
starters:
The bodega on the corner of Tenth Avenue has its shutter half up and a hand-lettered sign taped inside the glass: CASH ONLY, NO EXCEPTIONS, ASK ZEKE. Ezequiel Rivas is behind the counter with his reading glasses on their cord, writing in a ledger with a pencil he sharpens with a pocketknife between entries. Four padlocked storefronts stand across the avenue, the chains bright and new.

He pushes a stool out with his foot without looking up. 'Sit,' he says, nodding at the stool by the coffee urn. 'You look like the city.'

A man in a grey work jacket comes in, nods to Zeke, and leaves a folded envelope under a can of peaches. Zeke does not touch it. He keeps writing, slowly, and the pencil stops on a name you half recognise from the campus flyers. Outside, a black sedan idles at the hydrant and does not move.

Zeke turns the ledger toward you, open to Friday. 'Read that,' he says. 'Then tell me if you know who wrote it.'

After midnight the dorm courtyard is the quietest place on campus. The lamps buzz over the benches, and the library's back windows are the only other lit thing on Eighth Avenue. Your roommate, Nia Oduya, is asleep under a lab coat on the top bunk, or pretending to be, with her phone glowing face down on the blanket.

From the window you can see the roof of the old annex across the courtyard. Gwen Stacy sits on its parapet with her legs hanging over the edge, hood down, short blonde hair catching the sodium light. She has been there for twenty minutes, looking at the street and not at the building.

Then she turns her head and looks straight up at your window, as if she has known the light was on the whole time. She lifts one hand, slowly, and holds it there, waiting to see whether you will wave back.

The plaza below Avengers Tower is cold even in September, and the wind comes off the river between the glass. The granite wall of names runs the length of the plaza, and tonight someone has left a fresh candle at the foot of it, still lit under a jar. Mary Jane Watson crouches beside the candle with her camera on a strap, shooting the names one by one at a low angle so the carved letters throw shadows.

She looks up when you step onto the paving stones, and her grin arrives a half second late. 'Hey. Don't tell me you came down here for the view,' she says. 'Everybody comes for the view and nobody reads the wall.' She turns the lens cap over in her fingers. Across the plaza, the tower's lobby lights are on their timer, the way they have been every night since the attack.

She stands and offers a folded printout of a blog post, the headline circled in pen: WHO IS PAYING KINGPIN'S COLLECTORS? Then she waits for your answer.

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 19, a sophomore at Empire State University in Manhattan. You share a dorm room with Nia Oduya and work evening shifts at Zeke's bodega on Tenth Avenue to cover your rent. You are not a hero, and nobody has asked you to be one. But the city's only protection wears spider-suits, the villains have noticed, and you have started seeing the same faces on the same rooftops.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
The Spider-Heroes - the spider-powered people who answer the city's calls, loosely networked, who want the city to last until it can go back to normal.
Wilson Fisk's Collectors - the criminal money of Hell's Kitchen, who want every shop in the district paying weekly and nobody watching.
Oscorp - the labs, warehouses and medical contracts the city depends on, who want their emergency contracts renewed and the street stim left unexamined.
The Dockside Crew - the Brooklyn waterfront gang and the ferry trade, who want the harbor and its boats to themselves.

entries.title: New York After the Attack
entries.content: New York City, present day. Thanos came with his army and killed every Avenger who was not a spider-person, Tony Stark, Steve Rogers and Thor among them. Avengers Tower stands empty over Midtown. The city runs on what is left: subways on a cut timetable, police stretched past what they can cover, and a few spider-people who answer every call they can reach.

entries.title: Who Holds the Line
entries.content: Only spider-powered people still stop serious crime in New York. The police, the National Guard and the civilian emergency panel all depend on them to show up when it counts. Nobody can order a spider-person to patrol, so when they are stretched thin, whole blocks go unguarded, and the villains have learned to move into the gaps the same night.

entries.title: Empire State University
entries.content: Empire State University is a brick campus of eleven buildings on the far west side of Midtown, where the avenues run up toward Hell's Kitchen. Classes still run, slower than before and with half the faculty gone. Students live in dorms on Eighth and Ninth Avenues. The library and the gym are the last places many of them feel safe after dark. Pryce Hall is the big lecture building on the north side, where Peter Parker teaches physics to a room that always looks cold.

entries.title: The Spider-Heroes
entries.content: The spider-powered people of New York are a loose network, not an army. Peter Parker takes the most calls. Miles Morales holds Brooklyn, Gwen Stacy patrols the rooftops across the west side, and Spider-Man 2099 and Scarlet Spider come and go from the other boroughs. They do not agree on methods and rarely meet in one place. They want the city to last long enough to find its way back to normal.

entries.title: Wilson Fisk
entries.content: Wilson Fisk, called the Kingpin, controls the criminal money of Hell's Kitchen and has spent the months since the attack taking the blocks nobody is watching. His collectors take a weekly cut from shops and padlock the ones that refuse. They send word to the spider-heroes' hotline before they move, to see who answers. Fisk himself has not been seen in public since the attack. People say he is waiting for the spider-heroes to get tired.

entries.title: Hell's Kitchen
entries.content: Hell's Kitchen runs from Ninth to Eleventh Avenue, with walk-up tenements over corner stores and the river smell in summer. Tenth Avenue is its spine: bodegas, laundromats, a shuttered theater, and the new padlocks on the shops that refused to pay. Residents talk to each other, not to the police. Fisk's collectors drive black sedans and never park for long.

entries.title: The Memorial
entries.content: The memorial is a long wall of grey granite on the plaza below Avengers Tower, carved in the weeks after the attack and added to by hand since. It lists the Avengers who were not spider-people and the civilians who died beside them. People leave candles, photographs and worn pieces of costume at its foot. A sign-in book sits in a glass box, and whoever keeps it writes down every visitor.

entries.title: Avengers Tower
entries.content: Avengers Tower rises over the East Side of Midtown, glass and steel, with its landing pad empty and its lobby lights on a timer. Nobody has moved the team's things out. The city keeps it lit at night as a monument, and nobody lives or works inside. Tourists come with flowers and leave with photos of the plaza. Some say the tower's security system still answers to its old owners, and nobody has found out who they are.

entries.title: The Attack
entries.content: Thanos came to New York with his army in one week that people now call the attack. The Avengers who were not spider-powered fought at the tower and in the streets, and every one of them died. The spider-people lived because they were scattered across the rooftops and the tunnels, and the fighting did not reach them in time. The official death toll is a figure people argue about in every bar.

entries.title: The Daily Bugle
entries.content: The Daily Bugle still prints from a Midtown newsroom with half its desks empty. Its editors run the official toll and the city's statements, and they put the spider-heroes on the front page as heroes and on the back page as menaces. Mary Jane Watson's independent blog outsells the Bugle among people who walk the streets at night, because her photographs are not cut to suit anyone's stake.

entries.title: Oscorp
entries.content: Oscorp owns the labs, warehouses and medical contracts that the city's emergency board relies on. Harry Osborn has run it since his father's death. It is the only company still shipping stimulants and healing compounds in bulk. The street version of the stim, sold cheap in Hell's Kitchen, traces back to an Oscorp building that is still on the company's books under another name.

entries.title: The Underworld
entries.content: With the Avengers gone, the gangs stopped fearing the city. The Dockside Crew runs the Brooklyn waterfront and the ferry trade. Fisk's collectors work Hell's Kitchen. Smaller crews hold parts of Queens and the Bronx. They trade in stim, protection, stolen power cells and information. They answer to nobody but the money, and each crew watches the others for the moment one of them looks weak.

entries.title: The Boroughs
entries.content: Manhattan keeps the city's money and the last full power grid. Brooklyn is Miles Morales's patch and the home of the Dockside Crew. Queens is quiet and partly dark, with its bridges watched day and night. The Bronx has the worst of the crews. Staten Island is cut off most nights because the last ferries stop at dusk.

entries.title: The Rooftops
entries.content: The rooftops are the city's real streets now. Routes run across them from campus to the Hudson piers and the Brooklyn Bridge, and a spider-person can cross a block in the time a car takes to turn a corner. Students see the flicker of suits between buildings after midnight and learn to keep their blinds closed. A person on a roof at night is either protected or being watched.

entries.title: Names in the City
entries.content: Names here come from the streets and the old families: Irish, Italian, Puerto Rican, Dominican, Korean, Nigerian, Greek and Chinese names sit on the same blocks, such as Rivas, Calderon, Park, Doyle, Moretti, Dimitriou and Chen. Use the name a person would give at a door. In Hell's Kitchen people are often known by their corner or their shop. Blocks and halls are named for an avenue and a number, a saint or an old donor.

world.vibe: tense and tired, warm at the edges; people deflect with jokes and settle debts with favors, and nobody says the thing they are afraid of

opening.note: Staged, over the first few turns. Beat one: Pryce Hall, the minute before the bell. Establish the wet wool, the blackboard, the wall screen with its padlocks on Tenth Avenue, and Peter Parker's scraped knuckles. Peter speaks first. He asks the player to stay behind and wants to know whether they have seen Miles Morales near the gym lockers, and he will not say why. Beat two: the interruption is Miles himself, who comes back with a police-band radio clipped to his bag and says Brooklyn has three calls in the same hour. Peter takes the radio, says nothing else, and leaves by the side door. Beat three, by the third turn: the player is left facing two doors. One leads down the hall to Ines Calderon's office, where she is waiting with a folder of patrol maps. The other leads to Tenth Avenue, where Ezequiel Rivas has the ledger open to a name he will not say aloud. Keep Gwen Stacy off the page until the player goes up to a roof or a window at night. Keep Mary Jane Watson's blog in the background until someone mentions the paid tips. Let the city be loud and the people be tired.

cast.name: Peter Parker
cast.role: Physics lecturer at Empire State University, and Spider-Man of Queens, carrying the city's emergencies on top of a full teaching load.
cast.look: lean and tired, a few days of stubble, grey scrapes on the right knuckles, sleeves pushed past the elbows, a cheap wristwatch he checks too often.
cast.manner: Speaks in the careful cadence of a lecture, slow and clean, and writes his point on whatever is nearest, a napkin, a sleeve, a fogged window. Says 'let's say' when he has already decided.
cast.secret: The stimulant Oscorp ships to the city's emergency responders is the same batch that keeps him upright on patrol, and his heartbeat has started skipping on the stairs. He has not told Gwen, Miles or Harry, and he is rationing the doses he has left.

cast.name: Gwen Stacy
cast.role: Spider-Woman who patrols the rooftops across the west side of Manhattan, sometimes from a world where the spider-people did not all survive.
cast.look: tall, short blonde hair, a hooded suit in white and blue faded at the knees, pale eyes that catch streetlight and do not blink much.
cast.manner: Clipped and sure, talks from a rooftop edge with her back half turned. Makes a joke, then asks you a plain question and watches your hands while you answer.
cast.secret: She has been watching your dorm because two of Kingpin's collectors asked the night desk who keeps the fourth-floor light on. She suspects someone in your building is talking to them, and she has not decided whether she can trust you.

cast.name: Miles Morales
cast.role: Spider-Man of Brooklyn and, at fifteen, an early-admission student at Empire State University on a science scholarship, who sits near you in Pryce Hall and cannot keep both jobs.
cast.look: compact and quick, close-cropped hair, a black hoodie with a faint red spider on the chest, a phone with a cracked corner that buzzes all day. Warm brown skin and a small scar through one eyebrow.
cast.manner: Talks fast and funny, then stops mid-sentence to listen to something only he can hear, usually the police band. Hums the same four bars when he is nervous.
cast.secret: He keeps a second suit folded in a gym locker at ESU because he cannot get home between Brooklyn calls. He is failing two classes and has not asked anyone for help, not even Peter.

cast.name: Mary Jane Watson
cast.role: Runs the independent news blog that tracks the spider-heroes, and sells the only honest photographs of them in the city. Pulls favors from every newsroom still standing.
cast.look: red hair up in a clip, a leather jacket over a silk blouse, a camera strap across her chest, bright eyes that have seen too many funerals this year.
cast.manner: Warm, fast and always deflecting with a joke that lands a little too hard. Ends hard questions with 'anyway' and changes the subject to someone's shoes.
cast.secret: The most reliable tip on her blog about Kingpin's movements comes from Nia Oduya, who lives in your dorm and sells what she hears for cash. Mary Jane pays in advance and has never asked where Nia gets it.

cast.name: Harry Osborn
cast.role: Runs Oscorp since his father's death, and sits on the city's emergency supply board, which hands out the medical stims.
cast.look: neat dark suit, a tired face made tidy by effort, a Swiss watch, and one bare hand that he keeps flat on the table.
cast.manner: Polite, precise and slow, speaks of the board as though it were weather. Never raises his voice, and answers a threat with the date of the next board meeting.
cast.secret: The street stim sold in Hell's Kitchen was made in an Oscorp warehouse that is still on the books under a shell company. Harry found the invoices six weeks ago and has not reported them, because the board is paid by the same shell.

cast.name: Ezequiel Rivas
cast.role: Owns the bodega on the corner of Tenth Avenue in Hell's Kitchen, where the block's rent and rumors get settled. Knows who collected from whom, and what it cost.
cast.look: heavy-set, grey beard trimmed close, a green apron over a pressed shirt, reading glasses on a cord, forearms marked with old burn scars from a stove.
cast.manner: Speaks softly in short, even sentences, and keeps writing in his ledger while you talk, stopping only when you tell him something he did not know.
cast.secret: He has paid Kingpin's collector every Friday for eleven years, and the payments buy the block's silence and keep his nephew, who is twenty-four, off a list. He has begun to think the list is being used for something worse.

cast.name: Ines Calderon
cast.role: Professor of urban history at Empire State University, and the civilian clerk who draws the patrol zones for the emergency panel that sends the spider-heroes where they are needed.
cast.look: small and upright, grey-streaked black hair in a knot, a cardigan with ink on one cuff, half-moon glasses on a beaded chain.
cast.manner: Precise and courteous, writes her points on index cards and reads them out in order, even when the room objects. Never says 'I think'. Says 'the record shows'.
cast.secret: She has been selling the patrol maps to Kingpin's lawyers, because they are the only people who paid for her mother's hospital bill. She tells herself the maps are a month out of date by the time they reach them.

cast.name: Nia Oduya
cast.role: Your roommate, a chemistry major who sells what she overhears on the Hell's Kitchen streets to anyone who pays, and who keeps the sale quiet from you.
cast.look: small and sharp-faced, a buzz cut dyed purple at the ends, a scarf knotted over a lab coat she never takes off, a phone always at four percent battery.
cast.manner: Talks in quick lowercase bursts, mostly half-finished, and ends with a question she does not want answered. Warms to you only after checking who else is listening.
cast.secret: She is Mary Jane Watson's source for the Kingpin stories, and she has been reading your messages, your study notes and your bank app to find things worth selling. She has not told you because she has not decided whether you are a risk.

systems.label: Awareness
systems.meaning: How much the spider-people and the villains have noticed you. Low means you are a student nobody has looked at twice. High means someone has your name in a file.
systems.change: Up when you are seen near a fight, a sealed file or a person Kingpin is watching. Down after a few quiet days on campus.

systems.label: Danger Level
systems.meaning: The threat in the blocks you move through: the padlocked shops, the collectors, the raids in Brooklyn.
systems.change: Up with each block Fisk takes, each collector sighting, and each night the spider-heroes are stretched too thin. Down when a patrol holds a block for a whole night.

systems.label: Community Trust
systems.meaning: How much the people of your building and your block will tell you the truth, and what they will do for you.
systems.change: Up when you help without being asked or keep a neighbor's secret. Down when you hand someone to the collectors or sell their name.

npcSystems.label: Trust
npcSystems.meaning: How far this person trusts you with what they know.
npcSystems.change: Up when you keep a secret they gave you or do what you said you would. Down when you sell one or lie to them.

style.art: Comic-book ink and halftone in saturated reds, blues and sodium-yellow streetlight; rooftops, webbing and glass towers, with ordinary students and spider-heroes in the same frame.

heroes.name: Sun-hee Park
heroes.description: A freshman from Flushing who runs a late-night campus radio show that reads out the names of the missing.
heroes.look: small and quick, black hair cut in a blunt bob, headphones around the neck, a university windbreaker with the sleeves pushed up, ink on the back of one hand from writing down call-ins.
heroes.background: Her family lost a cousin in the attack week. She started the show from a dorm closet because the station needed someone and nobody else would stay up. Callers trust her with things they will not tell the police, and she records every call and keeps the recordings on a drive she wears round her neck.
heroes.carries: A portable radio, a lanyard with her station keycard, and a pocket recorder with a cracked case.

heroes.name: Jonah Adair
heroes.description: A materials PhD student who spent the attack week sealed inside a lab and has been trying to build a better power cell since.
heroes.look: tall and thin, sunburned neck, ink-stained fingers, a grey hooded work jacket scorched at the cuffs.
heroes.background: He was two weeks from his defense when the attack came, and his advisor never came back from a meeting in Midtown. Jonah keeps a coil of test filament in a pill bottle, a first cut at a working battery for the emergency lines, and he has not slept through a night since.
heroes.carries: A lab keycard, a multimeter, and a pill bottle of tungsten filament.

heroes.name: Efe Dimitriou
heroes.description: An ESU student who worked nights as a guard at Avengers Tower and still keeps the memorial's sign-in book.
heroes.look: lean and watchful, close-shaved head, a navy guard's jacket with the patch torn off the shoulder, reading glasses pushed up on the forehead.
heroes.background: The tower's guards were let go the month after the attack, and nobody paid the last check. Efe still walks the plaza at night, writes down everyone who leaves a flower, and knows which lobby lights have gone out.
heroes.carries: A flashlight, the sign-in book, and an old guard radio that still picks up dispatch.
